headline: Why DIY Drain Cleaning Can Make Things Worse
articleBody: It's totally tempting to grab a bottle of chemical drain cleaner or try that internet hack when your sink starts draining slowly. We get it, it seems like a quick and easy fix. But honestly, those seemingly simple solutions can often lead to bigger, more expensive headaches down the line. Chemical cleaners, for example, are super corrosive. While they might eat through a clog, they can also damage your pipes, especially older ones, leading to leaks or even bursts. Plus, they often don't fully clear the blockage, just create a small path, meaning the clog will be back in no time. Then there's the risk of injury if those chemicals splash back. For more stubborn clogs, a simple plunger just won't cut it and might even push the blockage further into your system. When you're dealing with persistent or multiple clogged drains, it's really best to call in a professional. We've got the right tools, like drain snakes and hydro-jetting equipment, and the know-how to clear the clog safely and effectively without damaging your plumbing.
